There is also correspondence between the principals to: clarify college rules, (in particular following a student request for permission to attend dances outside of the college and regarding the decision to invite a male speaker), arrange debates (which include a debate over the value of militancy in the British women's suffrage movement and debates against the women's colleges at Cambridge and at a local school), arrange hockey and tennis fixtures, establish quarantine protocols and arrange chaperones. The volume also includes a 'Directory of Women Teachers', and letters between college principals to decide the official position on student suffrage involvement, along with a rough contents page at the beginning of the volume.

Manuscript IV, including unidentified tracts on propositions, universals, inception, denominations and proportions, six logical tracts by Richard Lavenham, and a question (ff. 116–170). Manuscript V, including John Tarteys's Problema correspondens libello Porphyrii (ff. 171–195).

Over the life-span of its publication, contents include an ‘Editorial Note’, a number of dramatic sketches, plays written by women, a ‘Correspondence’ section and reports from the following: Oxford Students’ Debating Society, Oxford Students’ Hockey Team, Oxford Students’ Lawn Tennis Club, Oxford Students’ Dramatic Reading Club, The AEW, Somerville College, Lady Margaret Hall, St Hugh’s Hall, St Hilda’s Hall, the Society of Oxford Home-Students, Oxford Women Students’ Society for Women’s Suffrage, Oxford University Co-operative Society, Oxford University Fabian Society, Historical Club.
